examples.solution_text:
Keep the negative substitution in brackets.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}Q(-2)\\&=(-2)^{4}+2(-2)^{3}-3(-2)+2\\&=16-16+6+2\\&=8\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Without substituting into every term, write down $P(0)$ for $P(x)=5x^{4}-2x^{3}+7x-6$.
examples.solution_text:
Every term containing $x$ becomes $0$, leaving the constant term.
$P(0)=-6$

examples.question_text:
a. Given $P(x)=(x-3)(x+4)(x+1)$, evaluate $P(-2)$.
b. Find the $y$-intercept of $y=(x+2)(x-4)(x+1)(x-2)$.
examples.solution_text:
a. Substitute into each factor without expanding.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}P(-2)\\&=((-2)-3)((-2)+4)((-2)+1)\\&=(-5)(2)(-1)\\&=10\end{aligned}$
b. At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.
$\begin{aligned}y&=(0+2)(0-4)(0+1)(0-2)\\&=(2)(-4)(1)(-2)\\&=16\end{aligned}$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,16)$.

First evaluate the required polynomial values.
$\begin{aligned}P(3)&=(3)^{2}-2(3)=3\\Q(-2)&=3(-2)+2=-4\\P(-1)&=(-1)^{2}-2(-1)=3\\Q(2)&=3(2)+2=8\end{aligned}$
a. $\begin{aligned}P(3)+Q(-2)&=3+(-4)\\&=-1\end{aligned}$
b. $\begin{aligned}P(-1)-Q(2)&=3-8\\&=-5\end{aligned}$
c. $\begin{aligned}(P(3))^{2}+(Q(-2))^{2}&=(3)^{2}+(-4)^{2}\\&=9+16\\&=25\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Given $P(x)=ax^{3}+5$ and $P(2)=37$, find $a$ and hence write $P(x)$.
examples.solution_text:
Substitute $x=2$ and use the given value.
$\begin{aligned}a(2)^{3}+5&=37\\8a+5&=37\\8a&=32\\a&=4\end{aligned}$
Therefore, $P(x)=4x^{3}+5$.

coverage.summary: Authored seven examples covering all distinct assessed methods, including factored y-intercepts and combinations of squared values. Used different source values, separate editable prompts and solutions, single-dollar mathematics and appropriate equals gutters. Solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. No diagrams are needed for these evaluation tasks. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged; independent review of the new examples remains required.

examples.derivation: At x=0, all nonconstant terms vanish, so P(0)=−6.
P(1/2)=8(1/8)+12(1/4)−4(1/2)+3=1+3−2+3=5. This adapts the supplied fractional substitution calculation without introducing remainder-theorem reasoning.
For part a, P(−2)=(−5)(2)(−1)=10. For part b, x=0 gives y=(2)(−4)(1)(−2)=16, so the y-intercept is (0,16). Both use direct substitution into factors.
P(2)=37 gives 8a+5=37, hence 8a=32 and a=4. Therefore P(x)=4x³+5; substitution yields 32+5=37.
